say: Galaxies are flat. [0.45] ~The thing holding them together is not.
Watch one form, in a real simulation. One spinning cloud of gas, and dark matter.
Gas particles collide. They heat up, shine, and lose their energy.
But spin can not be lost. [0.5] ~So the gas snaps flat.
Dark matter never collides. It keeps its energy, [0.3] and stays a big round cloud.
That is the only difference in this simulation. [0.4] One kind of particle collides. One does not.
Not every galaxy is flat. When galaxies crash together, a disk can be scrambled.
So the bright disk we see [0.3] is the small flat part of something far bigger. [0.6] ~A giant ball we can not see.
